notes: RECONSTRUCTED (not contemporary) key: Satoshi Tomokiyo's reconstruction of the Bishop of Rennes cipher (1561-1564), BnF Colbert 390, published on cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/henryiii.htm ('Bishop of Rennes (1561-1564)' section). Tomokiyo states: 'The King and Queen Mother used the same ciphers as far as the specimens here are concerned' - the only one of his Charles IX/Catherine-era keys he explicitly ties to Catherine. Row 1 = primary glyph per plaintext letter (22 headers: a b c d e f g h i l m n o p q r s t u x y z; no j,k,v,w). Homophone rows exist under most letters (transcribed below as uncertain). CONFLICT with the lane's Lasry-derived table (data/charlesIX-key-table.json): Rennes row 1 maps cipher 'h'->plain 'b', while the interlinear alignment gave cipher 'h'->plain 'E' (certain). The two tables cannot both be the du Croc key for glyph 'h'. Word/nomenclator pink rows ('bien com con dit ...', 'mais nous ont par ...', "'Empereur Roy de Boheme") were NOT transcribed (out of scope for glyph-inventory comparison). Cipher glyph tokens used here are the lane's ASCII approximations from data/medici-1567-cipher.txt (e.g. '#' = double plus, 'B' = 2beta ligature, 'J' = long-s/integral, 'H' = phi-like, 'C' = epsilon-like).
